newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nerves, Wall Street undercut Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Nerves, Wall Street undercut Brussels bourse.

text.p: Nerves, holidays, a lower trend on Wall Street and rising short-term interest rates undercut the Brussels bourse on Tuesday, with the immediate direction unclear but the longer-term uptrend intact, traders said.
The Bel-20 index ended a largely flat day down 11.61 points, or 0.46 percent, at 2,489.71.

There were 14 blue-chip losers. The six gainers included chemicals and pharmaceuticals firm UCB and electronics firm Barco, which bucked the trend to clock up strong gains for the second successive day.
"We are cautious for the short term. Perhaps the rise has been a bit overdone," one trader said. "But for the longer term we remain fundamentally positive."
Traders said the day's decline would have been larger had it not been for aggressive buying by one player of every share offered in UCB.

"We do not know who it is, but every time a UCB share is offered it is snapped up," one trader said. "It is true that the first-half figures are expected to be very good, but there must be something more behind this buying than pure speculation."
UCB reports first half results on July 30.
UCB ended up 1.8 percent at 137,600 francs, having earlier set a 1997 high of 140,000 francs.

Barco added 1.2 percent to close at 7,700 francs, having also set a year high of 7,720 francs on 'buy' recommendations following positive assessments of its purchase last week of Danish audio and videa firm RE.
However, the two shares were among the few stars of an otherwise overcast day on the bourse.
Banque Bruxelles Lambert dropped 2.9 percent to 9,510 francs on what traders said was an assessment that the share was now overpriced.
Shipper CMB fell 2.7 percent to 2,530 francs although traders said they were at a loss to explain why given the positive impact on the company of the strong dollar.
Elsewhere the declines were attributed largely to profit-taking.
"Everyone is becoming a bit more cautious," one trader said.
